html:
King of Babylon from about 1792 to 1750 BCE, sixth of an Amorite dynasty. He turned Babylon from one city-state among many into the head of the Old Babylonian kingdom, which ruled most of Mesopotamia.

For most of his reign he played a careful game of alliances. In his last fifteen years he struck: he beat Elam, took Larsa in the south, then turned on his old ally Zimri-Lim and destroyed Mari. Thousands of letters from Mari's archive show the diplomacy of the age.

He is best known for the Code of Hammurabi, about 282 laws carved on a black stone stele under an image of the king before the sun god Shamash, god of justice. Its rules, such as "an eye for an eye" with penalties that depended on class, follow older codes like the Code of Ur-Nammu. The stele was carried off to Susa as loot and found there in 1901. Babylon's god Marduk rose with the city. The kingdom shrank after his death and fell when the Hittites sacked Babylon around 1595 BCE.
